solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hymn about suffering parenticidal attack?

definitions.meaning: a Latin hymn on the sorrows of the Virgin Mary at the Cross
split 4,2,5 it reads as a knife-thrust at a mother (Latin mater), an assault by someone killing a parent

explanation.surface: Someone describes a hymn about suffering, then jokes about a violent assault on a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: split as STAB AT MATER, the title becomes a stab at one's mother, mater being Latin and old public-school slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval Latin sequence, often set to music, meditates on Mary's grief at the Crucifixion.

clue.text: Shaken + stirred, use dash of rum in it = cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is shaken and stirred, both signalling that the gathered letters are mixed up
a dash is a small first splash, so only the opening letter of rum is used

parts.note: the printed sign is read out as its word, the same as the answer to 19 across

explanation.surface: A bartender's recipe in shorthand: shake and stir, add rum, and the result is a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbols are clue words: '=' supplies EQUALS (the 19 across answer) to go into the anagram, while '+' is just part of the instruction to shake and stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila sunrise is a mixed drink of tequila, orange juice and grenadine, a standard cocktail.

clue.text: Buzzer's what contestant may press to fill rapidly emptying pot

parts.note: a bee is the buzzing insect

indicators.note: one piece is put inside to fill the gap left in the other
emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: a quiz contestant presses a bell to answer

explanation.surface: A quiz scene: a contestant hits the buzzer while some pot is quickly emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' looks like the quiz buzzer but is the insect; 'emptying' keeps only the outside letters of 'rapidly', and 'to fill' puts the contestant's bell between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot or pot belly is a protruding stomach, and one blamed on drinking ale is so called.

clue.text: Number One is Home featuring King Creole …

indicators.note: a thing featuring something has it included, so the letter for King goes in

parts.note: number one in the charts is at the top
K is the chess abbreviation for king
being home is being in

explanation.surface: A chart headline: Elvis's King Creole is number one, as if from a list of hits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Creole' reads as the Elvis film and song, but King gives K and Creole alone is the definition; the ellipses link a run of pop-themed clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Tok Pisin is the English-based creole spoken widely in Papua New Guinea.

clue.text: … the essence of Spandau Ballet and Sade's Here Comes the Sun? …

indicators.note: the essence is the core, so the central three letters of each act's name are taken

explanation.surface: Music talk: what lies at the heart of two eighties acts, with a Beatles title thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Spandau Ballet and Sade were 1980s British pop acts. The three central letters of SPANDAUBALLET give AUB, those of SADES give ADE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a song or poem greeting dawn, which a Beatles title about the sun rising illustrates.

clue.text: … top US rock band adding Writer's Award …

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the head, so the band name loses its first letter

parts.note: R.E.M. is the American rock band
the writer's means belonging to me

explanation.surface: A top American rock group picks up a songwriting prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like praise for the band but means behead.
explanation.definitionFit: This statuette is the annual US television prize for programmes and performers.

clue.text: … playing Blur and Blue gig without half of U2 is so namby‑pamby

indicators.note: the letters are played around with into a new order
the letters are what remains without the given piece
the first half of the band name is taken

explanation.surface: A music snob sneers that Blur and a Blue gig minus half of U2 is feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur and Blue are British pop bands. The letters of BLUR, BLUEGIG and ISSO, less a U (half of U2), are rearranged. A big girl's blouse is British slang for a weak or soppy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Namby-pamby means feeble or wet; the British insult describes such a weakling.

clue.text: Awful Hyde's mounting sixth sense, alter-ego blocking return to normal state

indicators.note: awful means bad, here mangling the letters
the alter ego blocks the passage by sitting inside the other piece
in a down clue mounting means going up, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception
an alter ego is another self, literally not I

explanation.surface: Mr Hyde's sixth sense grows, his alter ego Jekyll standing in the way of normality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hyde's' gives HYDE with 's as the link (has); 'mounting' turns ESP into PSE, which NOTI is 'blocking'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone out of a trance is to restore them to their ordinary waking condition.

clue.text: This, at intervals, makes guy maybe quite nervous?

indicators.note: nervous letters are jittery, shaken into a new order
letters taken at intervals are every other one

explanation.surface: An anxious remark that something makes a man fairly jumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-all-in-one: 'This' is the definition, and the whole clue describes it. MKSU (alternate letters of 'makes guy') with MAYBEQUITE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeaky-bum time is British football slang for the tense closing stage of a contest, so the clue's nervous moment is it.

clue.text: Carrier of code north I think carries partying women with knobs on

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards

parts.note: DNA carries the genetic code

indicators.note: one piece carries the other inside it

parts.note: to me means in my opinion
hens are women on a hen party

explanation.surface: A tangled sentence about genetics, a northern thinker, and women out partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I think' gives TO ME (as in 'to me, it looks wrong').
explanation.definitionFit: With knobs on is British slang for more so, and in abundance, the same idea as plus extra.

clue.text: Catch slow-mover, taking seconds

indicators.note: taking something away removes it

parts.note: a snail is a proverbially slow creature

explanation.surface: Catching a sluggish creature takes a moment or two.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a culprit is to catch or arrest them, an informal synonym.

clue.text: A day spent loading kids' pet after it gets return fare from Cornwall

indicators.note: the rest is placed after the first piece
a return reads the word back the other way
loading puts something inside, so the shortened day goes into the pet

parts.note: doggy is a child's word for a dog

indicators.note: spent means used up, so the stated letter is gone

parts.note: day as written

explanation.surface: A day spent feeding a child's dog before it gets the train fare back from Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like a train ticket but is food. 'spent' uses up the A in front of 'day', and what is left goes into the pet; 'after' puts all that behind the reversed 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Cornish dialect for a pasty, the county's best-known food.

clue.text: See 12
See 3
Help prepare treasure hunt for Spooner's terrier?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: to bury the prize helps set it up
a treasure hunt runs on clues

explanation.surface: Someone asks for help setting up a treasure hunt for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Help prepare treasure hunt gives BURY CLUE; swapping the opening sounds gives the dog breed, spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kerry blue is an Irish breed of terrier with a soft blue-grey coat.

clue.text: Some backed having extra facility for The Listener figures

indicators.note: backed means reversed, so the word runs right to left

parts.note: some is a part

indicators.note: for a listener the words are heard, not read, so their sound counts

parts.note: with extra ease is more easily, i.e. easier

explanation.surface: Puzzle talk: figures who find the Listener crossword easier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard Times crossword, but here it simply means someone hearing the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapezia are four-sided geometric shapes, plane figures.

clue.text: The Yard's Pen, her sister, experiencing heart flutter

indicators.note: a fluttering heart jumps about, so the two middle letters change places

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A Scotland Yard officer's female colleague, sister of another, has palpitations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Yard's Pen' suggests Scotland Yard, but it is a farmyard enclosure. The 'heart flutter' swaps the two central letters of her-plus-sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmyard pen where hens are kept is the exact sense, the enclosure being a hen run.

clue.text: Rarefied and sensational whatnot

parts.note: rarefied air is thin
gamy means racy or sensational

explanation.surface: Something both refined and sensational, an object that defies description.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are placeholder words for something whose name escapes you.

clue.text: What 2's parallel bars mean for peers

definitions.meaning: the sign of two short level bars in clue 2 down reads as a word saying the two sides are the same
peers are people of the same rank

explanation.surface: An oddity about gymnastic parallel bars in some second item and what they mean to peers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parallel bars' suggests gymnastics, but it is the '=' sign in 2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The = sign is read with this word, and one's peers are those of the same standing.

clue.text: Hungry mum knocked up repast

parts.note: mum means keep quiet, signalled by the call sh

indicators.note: something knocked up is roughly put together, a new arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A mother quickly throws together a meal for someone famished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother but means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp-set is an old phrase for keenly ravenous, with appetite sharpened.

clue.text: Love to try nibbling slice of duck (that's not very good!)

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a round letter

indicators.note: the word nibbles, taking the small piece inside it

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

indicators.note: a slice is a small bit, here the first letter

explanation.surface: A cook is told to try a bite of duck, and judges it disappointing.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation expresses mild dismay at something bad.

clue.text: The eccentric covering web activity's fine, of course

indicators.note: the new letters cover over the one meant by fine, replacing it

parts.note: surfing is browsing the web
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
the letters of The, made eccentric (rearranged), give a new order

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that an odd person's online browsing is quite acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges The into ETH, which covers (takes the place of) the F in SURFING.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are emphatic affirmatives meaning certainly.

clue.text: See 22
Extra meaning of 2's cross

definitions.meaning: an extra is an additional advantage
the small cross sign in clue 2 down is read as the word for addition

explanation.surface: A puzzle remark about an additional meaning of a cross in some second item.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross is the '+' sign in 2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: This means an advantage or bonus, and is also how the addition sign is read.

clue.text: A head teacher's detained

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the word, like a pupil kept in

explanation.surface: A school head is kept in, a teacher punished like a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging five pounds per person means 'so much apiece', i.e. a head.

clue.text: See 15
Time on average left in service? Perhaps us setters' pain may be relieved here

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic service
an age is a time
par is the norm, what one is on average
belonging to us, as setters say of their puzzles

explanation.surface: Setters joke that, after time spent averaging out, their own pain is soothed somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: This establishment offers rubs where aches are eased, though the phrase often hints at less innocent services.

clue.text: Being parched with sun delayed fair number

indicators.note: delayed means moved later, so the letter for sun shifts further along

parts.note: being parched is being in need of a drink
even means fair or balanced

explanation.surface: Someone is thirsty, the sun delayed, at a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a funfair but means level; 'delayed' sends the sun's letter further back in the word for parched.
explanation.definitionFit: It is simply a counting number, one more than thirty-six.
